methodology: Verse-level preliminary screening against Qur'an 12:21-25 and Hebrew Masoretic Genesis 39 as displayed with Revised JPS translation on Sefaria. No critical textual apparatus or dated witness collation; do not claim literary dependence or verified public references. Prior draft #425 inspected; main snapshot dated 2026-11-08 has 34 verified associations across 23 verses; RLS concern #93 unresolved.

verses.summary: Egyptian purchaser instructs wife to honor Joseph, anticipating benefit or adoption; Genesis 39:1-6 names Potiphar and reports Joseph's household advancement, not adoption.
Joseph reaches maturity and receives judgment and knowledge; Genesis 39:2-6 describes divine favor and success but not an equivalent formal bestowal of wisdom at maturity.
Household woman solicits Joseph behind closed doors; Genesis 39:7-10 has master's wife solicit him and Joseph reject her, invoking duty to master and God.

Qur'an describes divine proof averting indecency and uses conditional language about Joseph's inclination; Genesis 39:8-12 emphasizes his refusal and flight without this specific divine-sign formulation.

Woman tears Joseph's shirt from behind during flight and accuses him at door; Genesis 39:12-18 describes seized garment left in her hand and subsequent accusation, but not a torn-back shirt or meeting at door.

dossier.title: Joseph in the Egyptian household: patronage, temptation and garment
dossier.chronology: Genesis 39:1-6 describes Joseph purchased by Potiphar, prospering under divine favor and placed in charge of the house. Qur'an 12:21-22 describes the Egyptian purchaser's instruction to his wife and Joseph's maturation and receipt of judgment and knowledge. Genesis 39:7-18 and Qur'an 12:23-25 then narrate the wife's solicitation, Joseph's refusal and a garment-centered accusation, with distinct sequencing and details.

source_table.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic display with Revised JPS 2023 translation; critical edition and apparatus not inspected

dossier.similarities: Joseph enters an Egyptian elite household; his master's wife solicits him; he refuses; his clothing figures in the ensuing accusation.
dossier.differences: The Qur'an mentions prospective adoption, Joseph's granted knowledge, locked doors, a divine proof, torn shirt from behind and accusation at the doorway. Genesis names Potiphar, describes daily entreaties and Joseph's garment left in her hand, followed by an accusation to servants and husband.
dossier.witnesses: Hebrew MT text displayed; Greek Septuagint, Syriac Peshitta, manuscript variants and Jewish/Syriac retellings still require collation.
dossier.dating: The Hebrew Genesis tradition is pre-Islamic; textual composition/redaction dates must not be conflated with the dates of surviving MT, Greek and Syriac manuscripts. No manuscript date independently audited in this batch.
dossier.interpretations: Strong shared Joseph narrative, with notable differences in the garment scene and theology of resistance. Transmission route and direct dependence unestablished.
